steps.note: S2.3.1.1.1 states rows 0-1 subtract the readout of the old scratch, rows 2-5 add the new readout, rows 6-7 restore c,a, so the net change (JV+RG)x is independent of a,c.
S2.3.1.1.2 gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, side wires cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, zero for intersections zero or two, and self coefficient one.

The plan treats only the bit construction; the complex-case central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 and the side-wire cancellation of intersections zero and two never appear (the |S cap T|-1 in S2.3.1.3.1 is the label form, not this coefficient).
S2.3.1.1.3 gives (x,y) -> (x,y+x) -> (-y,y+x) -> (-y,x) via the inverse schedule X <- X-Y, each invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

The plan only asserts that every edge joins comparable labels and says S2.3.1.3.4 'lists every edge's orthogonal residual', but never states the residuals or their dimensions beyond the single center 3->4 edge.

S2.3.1.3.3 has the inclusion P(x)<t_X> in P(x)t_Y^perp from t_X perp t_Y (as the interstage pass-through, quote line 953), but not the side edge 2->5 residual, the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp, or its dimension h-2.
S2.3.1.3.4 gives center 3->4 as the only decreasing edge losing h, and S2.3.1.3.5 telescopes: sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed Wm-2N, absolute adds 2L.

No step says that over F_2 each nonzero residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating or that it has an orthonormal basis; S2.4.1.1 merely presupposes 'an orthonormal residual basis' without the argument or the absorption of alternating planes.
S2.3.1.3.6 gives L_b/N=100/539 and S2.4.1.2 gives L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2.

S2.4.1.1 states weight is additive mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors because supports meet evenly, hence q_V-q_U is a sum over an orthonormal residual basis (the explicit wt(v)[v.x] summand is only implicit via the phase i^{+-[v.x]}).

S2.4.1.1 asserts each phase is i^{+-[v.x]} and becomes aI+bX_v after 'Hadamard conjugation', but never states that wt(v) is odd (norm one) as the reason for the +-1 exponent, nor the identity H diag(1,-1) H = X.
The plan has one tensor-power kernel factor (C^{+-1})^{tensor f} per residual basis vector with s_c factors/child calls in all, though phrased on f axes rather than k columns.

No step gives the zero-label frame I and full-label frame C^{tensor m}, the X_a->Y_a pair carrying C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a), the Z_{a,k} and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} repair, or the negation of X outputs; S2.4.1.4 covers negative edge kernels only.
S2.3.1.4.3 states L_b<N/2, deficit N-2L_b>0 from W_b m, and s_b<W_b m (the complex side appears in S2.4.1.2).
The value eta_c = 73/19906842167500 appears nowhere in the plan.

S2.3.1.5 carries the chain eta exceeds 20*2^-50, log m<20, m^{1-2^-50}>m(1-20*2^-50)>m(1-eta), so s_b/W_b<m^tau with tau=1-2^-50, but only for the bit side (no eta_c or sigma=tau statement for the complex side).

S2.3.1.6.1 gives pivoting on the rightmost nonzero entry of the topmost nonzero row with lower-triangular clearing to get A=E_1 Pi E_2, and S2.3.1.6 says Pi has a ones; the repeat on active indices is only implicit.
S2.3.1.6.2 says the prime q avoids all denominators so the factors stay invertible modulo q^b, though without 'finite table' wording.
S2.3.1.6.2 states a lower-triangular change costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order since earlier coordinates still hold original values.
S2.3.1.6.3 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange of (H_i,D_j), then D_j<-H_i-D_j, one interchange per one of Pi and a in all.
S2.4.6 mentions C_1=20 and Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) but never defines E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu, C_0=128mB^2 or C_1=max{20,nu+3} with nu=11.
The recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at internal nodes and A(e)<=8e at leaves, and the per-invocation count below E, never appear; S2.4.6 merely asserts the depth is below C_0 d^{C_1}.
No unrolling B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu or A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1} appears; the plan only asserts the final depth bound in S2.4.6.

S2.4.6 asserts that p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits suffice and that Delta=o(p) because epsilon*C_1<1, but omits the depth-l claim (values in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] of modulus at most 2^l) that justifies exactness.
S2.4.7 states every row of H has absolute row sum one so disk arrays map to disk arrays and the single final truncation errs by less than sqrt2 * 2^-p.

summary: 15 of 26 present: B1, B2, B4, L3, L5, P1, P3, R1, R2, R4, M1, M2, M3, M4, S5. The plan covers the bit network, the L_b/L_c ratios, the eta_b chain, the matrix shear and the row-sum truncation, but omits the complex-case coefficients (B3), the residual table and h-2 complement (L1, L2), the F_2 orthonormal-basis argument (L4), odd weight and the endpoint 27-coordinate repair (P2, P4), eta_c (R3), and the whole arithmetic-depth derivation (S1-S4).
